_comment: Recorded NON-conformance of the eleven public read paths against the approved
project_only rule, as observed by tools/scope-conformance.mjs on the v0.41.0
kernel. Every row here is a known failure, not an expectation to keep: the
harness exits 0 only while each path still behaves exactly as recorded, and
refuses any row that already meets the target.
A row is retired -- deleted, with conformant assertions added to the
production suite -- by the change-set that makes its path conformant, never
edited to follow a behaviour change. Rows are grouped by the change-set
expected to retire them; the file is deleted once the last group is retired.
A retired path must meet its whole target: the unresolved half AND the
selected-project half.
The read boundary of all eleven paths is conformant and retired: the core
read paths (matchesFilters, search, retrieve, recall, context) by plan v1.4.4
PR-08; the by-id read (entity, through traverse) and traverse by PR-09;
getJournal, stats, redact and the public export by PR-10, each with the
target that no selected answer names the beta id of the cross-project link.
What an unresolved read reports about itself -- complete:false and a
scoped-coverage limitation -- is plan PR-11's, so it is checked separately
as <path>.coverage, for every path that returns a completeness envelope.
Those rows record that envelope as it stands before PR-11: the four core
rows as PR-08 left it, and getJournal's as PR-10 left it (which added the
scoped-coverage limitation of P1 reconciliation F-09 to every journal read,
but not complete:false). They are the last group; PR-11 retires them and
deletes this file.
Fixture: projects alpha and beta, plus a decision and a memory in the literal
project default (where identity-less writes landed until the schema-6 writer
refused them), and a deliberate cross-project link from an alpha decision to a beta
attempt, imported as the history it is since link() refuses one (PR-09).
'withheld' means the read was made with no project argument; 'selected' means
it was made with project alpha.
